Net treatment benefit, win ratio and win odds of prioritized endpoints

Source: R/WinStat.R
WinStat.Rd

Compares every patient of one cohort (treatment) with every patient of another cohort (control) on prioritized endpoints (generalized pairwise comparisons, Buyse 2010) and computes the net treatment benefit, the win ratio (Pocock et al. 2012) and the win odds (Brunner et al. 2021) with standard errors and confidence intervals.

Usage

WinStat(
  data,
  endpoints,
  treatment,
  control,
  group = "group",
  priority = NULL,
  threshold = NULL,
  scoring = c("gehan", "peron"),
  conf.level = 0.95
)

Arguments

data

Patient-level data frame with one row per patient.

endpoints

An Endpoint object or a list of them.

treatment, control

Names of the two cohorts compared, values of the column group.

group

Name of the column of data with the cohort.

priority

Character vector of endpoint names in decreasing priority; by default the order of endpoints.

threshold

Numeric vector of thresholds, one per element of priority: the minimal difference of times that decides a pair on a time-to-event endpoint (0 or NA for binary endpoints). By default 0 for every endpoint. The thresholds of an endpoint used more than once must decrease.

scoring

Scoring rule of time-to-event endpoints: "gehan" or "peron".

conf.level

Confidence level of the intervals.

Value

A list of class WinStat with elements

estimate

Named vector with p_win, p_loss, p_tie, ntb, wr and wo.

ci

Data frame with the estimate, standard error and confidence interval of the net treatment benefit (NTB), the win ratio (WR) and the win odds (WO).

by.endpoint

Data frame with, for each priority level, the proportions of all pairs won and lost at that level and the proportion of pairs still undecided after it (with the Peron scoring rule, sums of probabilities divided by the number of pairs).

n

Named vector with the numbers of treatment and control patients and of pairs.

settings

List with treatment, control, scoring and conf.level.

See WinStat-methods for print() and plot().

Details

A pair is compared on the endpoints in the order of priority. The first endpoint that decides the pair determines a win or a loss of the treatment patient; a pair that no endpoint decides is a tie. An endpoint can appear more than once with decreasing thresholds, for example with a large threshold first and a threshold of 0 later.

A binary endpoint decides a pair when the two patients have different values; a pair with a missing value is undecided. With scoring = "gehan", a time-to-event endpoint is scored by the rule of Gehan (1965): the pair is decided when the patient with the shorter observed time has an event and the difference of the observed times is at least the threshold. With a threshold of 0 the difference must be positive, and a censored time equal to an event time counts as longer. These rules agree with the Gehan scoring rule of the BuyseTest package.

With scoring = "peron", pairs with a censored time are scored by the rule of Péron et al. (2018). The true time of a censored patient is given the distribution of the Kaplan-Meier estimate of its cohort conditional on survival beyond the censoring time, and the pair is won with the probability that the treatment time is longer by at least the threshold and lost with the probability that the control time is longer by at least the threshold. The Kaplan-Meier estimate is not defined after the largest observed time of a cohort; the probability beyond that time counts only when the comparison holds wherever the true time lies, so the two probabilities are lower bounds, and the rest of the pair goes to the next endpoints. When an endpoint is used again with a smaller threshold, the probabilities at its previous threshold are subtracted, since a pair won at the larger threshold is also won at the smaller one, and the weight of a pair is the product over the other endpoints of the probability that the pair is still undecided. These rules agree with the Peron scoring rule of the BuyseTest package, except that a difference of times exactly equal to a positive threshold always counts as decided, which can give small differences when times plus or minus the threshold coincide with event times.

With p_win, p_loss and p_tie the proportions of pairs won, lost and tied by the treatment patient, the net treatment benefit is p_win - p_loss, the win ratio p_win / p_loss and the win odds (p_win + p_tie / 2) / (p_loss + p_tie / 2). Their standard errors are computed from the first-order H-decomposition of the two-sample U-statistics (Bebu and Lachin 2016), the standard errors of the win ratio and the win odds by the delta method. With scoring = "peron" the Kaplan-Meier estimates are treated as known, so the standard errors are approximate and tend to be too small. The confidence interval of the net treatment benefit is computed on the inverse hyperbolic tangent scale, that of the win ratio on the log scale, and that of the win odds is the interval of the net treatment benefit transformed by (1 + x) / (1 - x).

References

Buyse, M. (2010). Generalized pairwise comparisons of prioritized outcomes in the two-sample problem. Statistics in Medicine, 29, 3245-3257. doi:10.1002/sim.3923

Pocock, S. J., Ariti, C. A., Collier, T. J. and Wang, D. (2012). The win ratio: a new approach to the analysis of composite endpoints in clinical trials based on clinical priorities. European Heart Journal, 33, 176-182. doi:10.1093/eurheartj/ehr352

Brunner, E., Vandemeulebroecke, M. and Mütze, T. (2021). Win odds: an adaptation of the win ratio to include ties. Statistics in Medicine, 40, 3367-3384. doi:10.1002/sim.8967

Bebu, I. and Lachin, J. M. (2016). Large sample inference for a win ratio analysis of a composite outcome based on prioritized components. Biostatistics, 17, 178-187. doi:10.1093/biostatistics/kxv032

Gehan, E. A. (1965). A generalized Wilcoxon test for comparing arbitrarily singly-censored samples. Biometrika, 52, 203-223. doi:10.1093/biomet/52.1-2.203

Péron, J., Buyse, M., Ozenne, B., Roche, L. and Roy, P. (2018). An extension of generalized pairwise comparisons for prioritized outcomes in the presence of censoring. Statistical Methods in Medical Research, 27, 1230-1239. doi:10.1177/0962280216658320

See also

BenefitRisk, SimSelection

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(group = rep(c("Cohort1", "Cohort2"), each = 40),
                os_tte = rexp(80, log(2) / rep(c(18, 15), each = 40)),
                os_event = rbinom(80, 1, 0.6),
                response = rbinom(80, 1, rep(c(0.45, 0.30), each = 40)),
                ae = rbinom(80, 1, rep(c(0.35, 0.20), each = 40)))
eps <- list(Endpoint("OS", "tte", time = "os_tte", event = "os_event"),
            Endpoint("ORR", "binary", var = "response"),
            Endpoint("AE", "binary", var = "ae", higher.better = FALSE))
res <- WinStat(d, eps, treatment = "Cohort1", control = "Cohort2")
res$ci
#>   statistic estimate        se      lower     upper
#> 1       NTB 0.083750 0.1217134 -0.1550319 0.3132865
#> 2        WR 1.216129 0.3486585  0.6933366 2.1331194
#> 3        WO 1.182810 0.2899614  0.7315539 1.9124229
res$by.endpoint
#>   priority endpoint threshold      win     loss undecided
#> 1        1       OS         0 0.292500 0.315000   0.39250
#> 2        2      ORR         0 0.158125 0.026875   0.20750
#> 3        3       AE         0 0.020625 0.045625   0.14125

# response first, then OS with a threshold of 3 months
WinStat(d, eps, treatment = "Cohort1", control = "Cohort2",
        priority = c("ORR", "OS", "AE"), threshold = c(0, 3, 0))$estimate
#>    p_win   p_loss    p_tie      ntb       wr       wo 
#> 0.510000 0.326875 0.163125 0.183125 1.560229 1.448355 

# censored pairs scored with the Kaplan-Meier estimates
WinStat(d, eps, treatment = "Cohort1", control = "Cohort2",
        scoring = "peron")$estimate
#>       p_win      p_loss       p_tie         ntb          wr          wo 
#> 0.548955956 0.447661285 0.003382759 0.101294670 1.226275252 1.225423544
